review_scope: Targeted high-utility/common-looking phrase candidates; not a contiguous row-range and not a claim about the remaining bank.

decisions.reason: Useful temporal expression, but a beginner can express near-future meaning more transparently with simpler time words already available in the core curriculum.
Correlative/discourse construction; it adds clause-linking complexity beyond the current A1 calibration need.
Discourse-management formula rather than an essential beginner survival expression.
Productive topic/viewpoint phrase, but structurally and pragmatically broader than the present A1 target set.
Marked/emphatic interrogative with strong formal or classical associations; ordinary A1 questions can use مَنْ directly.
Short, highly reusable reassurance/acceptance formula in ordinary communication; teachable as a fixed chunk without advanced syntax.
Formal speech/letter transition and register-specific rather than everyday beginner language.
Common existential negation built from beginner-grade material and directly useful for simple place/existence statements.
Useful but replaceable at A1 by simpler immediate-time wording; no need to spend beginner phrase budget on it yet.
Degree-hedging expression requiring more abstract discourse control than current A1 passages need.
Formal agent/source construction; simple active clauses are more appropriate for A1.
Generalizing discourse phrase; not necessary for concrete beginner narratives.
Abstract certainty construction with embedded clause syntax beyond current A1 calibration.
Natural frequency phrase, but less transparent than simpler A1 frequency adverbs.
Necessity construction plus subordinate verb pattern adds avoidable grammatical load at A1.
Discourse transition/summarizer rather than essential concrete beginner language.
Clause-linking causal conjunction; current A1 cause relations can be expressed with simpler structures.
Contrastive discourse connector requiring multi-clause argument structure not needed in A1 calibration.
Natural but redundant with simpler beginner frequency expressions.
Common expression, but current A1 scheduling can use concrete time words such as غدًا before introducing the abstract noun المستقبل.
Abstract necessity phrase with subordinate syntax; substantially heavier than needed for A1.
Temporal subordinator requiring sequencing of two clauses; defer until clause-linking is established.
Aspectual 'about to' construction is useful but nonessential during first-stage A1 reading calibration.
Idiomatic temporal phrase; concrete clock/day sequencing is preferable at A1.
Evaluative construction with an embedded verbal clause; simpler adjective statements suffice at A1.
Situation-framing discourse phrase; current A1 passages can state the concrete situation directly.

guardrails: A1_eligible means permitted for deliberate beginner use; it does not mean learner-known or mastered.
not_A1_current_review is not a precise later-CEFR assignment.
